speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked	the Minister for Social and Family Development why there are three occupants in a 1-room rental unit in Senior Group Homes instead of the standard number of two occupants under the typical HDB rental housing scheme.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked	the Minister for Social and Family Development whether the Ministry will consider extending the Senior Group Home scheme to suitable adults with special needs whose families are no longer around or able to look after them.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Minister, do you want to take the next two questions together?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The Senior Group Home is an assisted living model where seniors can live independently in the community and provide mutual support to one another.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They are paired with their room-mates as buddies and they help to look out for each other.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The number of seniors per unit is determined by the rental unit's configuration, the seniors' mobility status and the use of assistive devices, such as a wheelchair.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Having three seniors staying together raises the level of mutual support, which is important as Senior Group Homes are not designed to provide round-the-clock care.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Such a configuration also takes into account the eventual demand for places as our population ages.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But having said that, the Senior Group Home operators are also learning from the actual experience.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is a relatively new set-up that we have put in place and we will look at feedback and what we are learning from it.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As we operationalise the scheme, if necessary, we will make adjustments along the way.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Seniors with special needs who are eligible for HDB public rental housing and are also suitable for communal living can be supported in the Senior Group Home.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: There are currently visually-impaired seniors in the Senior Group Homes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I have actual feedback from residents who are living in these Senior Group Homes or assisted living models that the arrangement where there are three tenants in one rental flat vs two tenants in a typical rental unit is really very crowded, especially, as the Minister has said, if wheelchairs are involved, and in the sharing of common facilities like the toilet in the rental unit.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I would really appreciate it if the Minister could take a look and examine this model again to see if this can just be on par with the occupancy number in a typical HDB rental flat and when it can be done.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For the next question, feedback received on the Senior Group Home as an assisted living model is actually very good.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And also to ask when the Minister can look into this and give us a response in the sector.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Third, there is also review that the current outcome of the Senior Group Home scheme does not seem to be as popular or as favourable as expected when it was first conceived and launched.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Perhaps the Minister would like to share his views on this.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I understand the concerns with regard to flat size.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The flats do vary in size and layout, and also, when there are wheelchairs and walking aids involved as well, we will have to take that into consideration.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The idea is this: in a regular rental flat, you have two people living in the flat and these are largely able-bodied individuals.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, not only just for the elderly, but whether this is a possible model for adults with special needs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is something that we are open to look at.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As mentioned, for the elderly space, we are looking at a whole range of different possibilities.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Some of these ideas may or may not work, but we want to try them because the numbers will be quite significant.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Managing of numbers and space allocation would be important, but we will experiment with the different possibilities.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For the special needs sector, not just for the elderly, as the Member mentioned, for adults with special needs, we will be quite happy to explore what are some of these options that we think might be useful for adults with special needs and whose families may not be able to look after them.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will be quite happy to engage the Member if she has specific ideas.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do have spare spaces, but that could be the result of this being a relatively new sort of arrangement that we are putting in place.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are open to new ideas as well, because I think providing support for our ageing population in various forms and at various stages of their own ageing process is very important.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, this is something that will be reviewed.
